questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose my study destination based on the opportunity to freely select courses taught in English, which aligned perfectly with my academic interests. Additionally, London appealed to me as a vibrant metropolis, far larger than Copenhagen, offering a unique blend of diverse cultures and perspectives. The city's dynamic environment and international character made it an ideal place for both academic and personal growth.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to find the information I needed upon arrival, thanks to the detailed emails that served as reminders and guides. KU was particularly good at providing clear information beforehand. However, I did encounter a challenge when one of my mandatory courses was unexpectedly not offered at the host university. This highlighted a lack of communication between KU and the host university. It would have been helpful if KU required the host university to have their course schedule finalized by a set deadline to avoid such issues arising after arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The host university had an incredibly competent exchange team that was 100% helpful and always available. Their presence and support made the arrival process seamless, and I have nothing but praise for how well everything was handled.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Finding off-campus housing was quite challenging, especially when trying to secure something affordable and livable. I would recommend starting the search as early as possible, joining Facebook groups dedicated to housing danish/swedish/norwegians people in London. KFUK also has some affordable options for danish people i London.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start looking for housing as early as possible, as the process can be time-consuming. While living in London is expensive, it’s comparable to Copenhagen in terms of pricing. London is an enormous city, and it can feel overwhelming at first, but don’t let that discourage you. Over time, you’ll find areas you love and develop a sense of belonging in those neighborhoods. Keep in mind that a semester is too short to explore the entire city, so focus on making the most of the places you enjoy.

questions.answer: I don’t recall many details about the registration process, which likely means it was smooth and straightforward. Everything seemed to fall into place without any significant challenges or complications.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All the help I needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: One of my mandatory courses was no longer offered when I arrived. This was a significant issue, as it disrupted my planned course schedule. Improved communication between the host university and the home university about course availability would have been helpful to avoid such situations.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don’t stress too much about registration. Both the host university and KU are there to support you, and things will work out one way or another, even if the process doesn’t go exactly as you expected. Be flexible and open to adjustments, and don’t hesitate to reach out for help if you encounter any issues.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses is somewhat easier compared to what we are used to at KU, particularly in terms of teaching methods and exams. While the material is engaging and educational, the teaching style often feels more like a high school environment. Classes tend to focus on open discussions and subjective opinions. However, I found this method beneficial as an exchange student, as the emphasis on oral participation helped me improve my English skills through frequent verbal practice.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style at my host institution was quite different from what I am used to at KU. At the host university, classes were more interactive, with a strong emphasis on open discussions and subjective opinions, creating a high school-like atmosphere. In contrast, KU places more focus on independent study and academic rigor. While the host university's approach felt less academically demanding, it was beneficial for me as an exchange student, as it allowed me to practice my English extensively through verbal participation and classroom dialogue.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
British Politics
Comparative Politics
International Relations of the Middle East

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would highly recommend International Relations of the Middle East, which I took as an elective. The course was incredibly interesting, offering a deep dive into the history of the Middle East—a topic I knew very little about beforehand. The discussions in class were particularly enriching, as many students had personal connections to the region and brought fascinating and diverse perspectives. The course is structured around key themes and actors in the region, providing a comprehensive and nuanced understanding of its dynamics.

Another great course was British Politics, also an elective. It was fascinating to study the British political system and compare it to Denmark’s. The differences between the two systems are significant and highlight unique aspects of each society. However, the course was challenging at times, as much of the background knowledge about British society was considered common knowledge by the other students, which I didn’t always share. Despite this, it was a highly rewarding course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries in supermarkets are much cheaper compared to Denmark, so if you have access to a kitchen, you can save a lot by cooking at home and bringing your own lunch to university. On the other hand, gyms in London are very expensive. However, Queen Mary has a fairly decent gym, and as a student, you can get a membership at a price similar to what you’d expect in Denmark, making it a good option for staying active.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were an incredible number of student societies covering everything from sports to hobbies and special interests, ensuring there was something for everyone. The university also had its own gym, which was a great facility for staying active. Additionally, there were plenty of social events, including many parties specifically organized for exchange students, making it easy to meet new people and feel part of the community.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend taking some time to travel around the UK. A visit to the Cotswolds, with its beautiful countryside and charming villages, offers a peaceful escape from city life. If you have more time, traveling to Scotland is an unforgettable experience, with stunning landscapes and a rich cultural heritage. Exploring these areas gives you a deeper appreciation of the UK beyond London and allows you to experience the country's incredible diversity.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend taking some time to travel around the UK.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the cultural and ethnic diversity in London. It’s incredible to experience such a vibrant mix of traditions, perspectives, and communities all in one place. It also made me reflect on how culturally homogeneous Denmark can feel by comparison, which was an eye-opening and valuable perspective to gain.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Just enjoy your stay and be as active s you can. The time runs up before you know it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.answer: To be a part of the vibrant city

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: London as a city felt a bit overwhelming at first.
